Hi Laura / ProcureTech team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood — excited to get the onboarding process started. To make the vendor activation as smooth as possible, can we schedule a 30-minute orientation/call to align on milestones, PO process, and the mutual action plan (MAP)? Below is a proposed agenda and a short checklist we’d like to cover on the call. I’ve attached the vendor onboarding form, our PO template, and a draft MAP for your review.

Proposed times (PT):
- Tue 9 Jun, 10:00–10:30
- Tue 9 Jun, 15:00–15:30
- Wed 10 Jun, 09:00–09:30

Draft agenda (30 min):
1) Introductions & roles (5 min)
2) Checklist review: onboarding form, tax/W9, insurance (5 min)
3) PO & invoicing flow: who issues PO, billing contact, invoice cadence (7 min)
4) MAP review: milestones, dates, owners (8 min)
5) Q&A & next steps (5 min)

Success criteria we aim for on this kickoff:
- PO issued and vendor code requested within 5 business days after call
- Onboarding form + compliance docs uploaded to shared Drive within 7 days
- Test send/invoice flow validated by finance within 10 business days

Please confirm which of the proposed times works or share alternatives. Also, could you confirm the primary billing contact and any internal stakeholders we should include on the MAP?

Attachments: vendor_onboarding_form.pdf, purchase_order_template.xlsx, mutual_action_plan.docx

Thanks,
—

Thanks Laura — putting a couple of notes on PO/invoice flow so we can cover them quickly on the call:

- Redwood AP routing: all invoices should be submitted to ap@redwood.com. Please include the PO number in the invoice PDF/metadata if available.
- PO issuance: Redwood typically issues a PO from Procurement after the vendor record is created and the onboarding form is completed. That means: vendor onboarding form -> vendor code request (Procurement) -> PO issuance.
- Required fields on invoice: vendor name, Redwood PO number, invoice date, tax ID, and line-level description matching the PO.
- Tax/compliance: W-9 for US entities or W-8BEN for foreign entities; we also request a certificate of insurance if services include on-site work (not the case for API SaaS, but good to confirm).

If you prefer, we can send a short PO checklist doc pre-call. I’ll be on the call to explain the procurement cadence and where the approvals typically sit.

—Ben
